flow.title: Record
flow.detail: Screen, voice, clicks and ⇧ ink on one clock

flow.title: Deliver
flow.detail: Clipboard and ⌥⇧V; no automatic session send

flow.title: Agent
flow.detail: The skill, then apparent zoom for a closer look

features.name: Animated homepage feature explanations
features.says: Four illustrative animations after the product video explain whiteboard feedback, the multimedia timeline, clipboard handoff, and an agent showing its changes in a captioned walkthrough. Animations pause offscreen and respect reduced motion.

features.name: Website link preview
features.says: Shared homepage links declare a minimal wide Apparent wordmark image for Open Graph and Twitter large-image cards, without requiring JavaScript.
features.note: Candidate only. Deployment and a fresh receiver unfurl are required; existing previews may remain cached.

features.name: Connect complete-bundle handoff
features.says: Explicit upload login queues new GUI captures without waiting for the network. Clipboard text includes a non-secret ID and remote fetch instruction while pending. A separate read login retrieves and validates the complete bundle; failures preserve the local original.
features.note: Default off; CLI sign-in only. Update Apparent for apparent connect; older apps use apparent cloud, retained as a compatibility alias. Connect browser routes at app.tryapparent.com/connect and /connect/device retain /hosted aliases; API, Google callback, host-only sessions and device credentials stay at hosted.tryapparent.com. The V4 web UI provides account sign-in, independent scope review and verified device approval; website approval does not prove local upload settings or CLI credentials. Native capsule, connection and recovery UI remain deferred. Candidate requires native capture/paste proof on each OS and deployed account approval. V1 rejects files above 90,000,000 bytes rather than omitting media. No automatic historical uploads. Explicit apparent connect upload creates a fresh ID; apparent connect retry keeps existing IDs. Better Auth migration candidate renews device credentials while renewal remains valid, preserving queued IDs and consent; revoked or expired renewal needs approval again. Existing credentials require one new login after updating. Service login does not establish encryption trust. Migration, live OAuth and both native platform gates remain required before release.

config.does: Enable the automatic upload queue only with experiment and consent
Record explicit permission to share capture contents

config.value: HTTPS API origin; loopback HTTP for development
config.does: Select the Connect account API, not a token or preference store

features.name: Share one recording by link
features.says: Copy link beside Paste reserves public-by-link access for the selected capture before its media finishes uploading. Settings exposes hosted account consent and shared-link management. CLI listing follows every page and revocation preserves the private recording.
features.note: Default off. Native candidate only: Linux GUI, macOS native pill/Swift Settings, onboarding cancellation, foreground clipboard gating and end-to-end real-feature walkthrough still require platform proof. A configured hosted API and explicit upload consent are required. Deployment also needs SHARING_ENABLED=true; it defaults off. No production deployment is implied.

features.name: Open the installed app by URL
features.says: The exact apparent://open URL opens the idle app without recording or sending. Active selection, recording and processing are left untouched. OS registration requires an updated app.
features.note: Default off. Candidate implementation: native browser-to-app proof is required separately on each OS; no website integration or installation detection is supplied.

features.name: Homepage team
features.says: The public homepage shows Olivia and Simon with uncropped portraits and links each affiliation logo to its organization.

features.name: Frog theatre feedback footer
features.says: Paper fades into the frog theatre behind a feedback invitation. Try first attempts apparent://open, then the same button offers an explicit second-click platform download; no installation detection or automatic download. Hero and footer share a rounded button style. The compact Berlin credit respects reduced motion; the LinkedIn chooser does not record or send feedback.

features.name: Interactive homepage belief
features.says: Scroll directly draws and reverses the work circle and enjoyable highlight. Me too sends one frog into a group hug; reduced motion skips travel. Mobile keeps text and controls inset with a compact text-to-frog gap.

features.name: Give Feedback…
features.says: Start a capture from the menu, review it locally, then open a GitHub feedback form. No capture data is added to the URL or uploaded automatically.

features.name: H.264 decoder setup warning
features.says: Warns when the Linux GStreamer runtime lacks H.264 decoding, gives a distro-specific repair command, and explains candidate-frame fallback in the capture summary.

features.name: Record the screen
features.says: Press the shortcut and Apparent records the display under the pointer once the keys come up, with a red edge glow as the cue.

shortcuts.does: Start or finish a capture (Alt+Shift+S on Linux)

features.note: The shortcut can be changed in Settings; on Omarchy an active Super+Shift+Copilot binding in bindings.lua takes precedence and is shown as managed by Hyprland.

features.name: Switch target as it starts
features.says: The capsule opens onto Area · Screen · iPhone for 3.5 s; a chip restarts the capture on that target.
features.note: The iPhone chip is Mac only. Window recording is temporarily disabled as containment for #230; #264 tracks safe restoration.

features.name: Choose What to Record…
features.says: The menu's picker opens on the pointer's display: drag an area, or pick Screen or iPhone.
features.note: Window recording is temporarily disabled on macOS and Linux, including record --window and direct recording entry points. There is no screen fallback. Existing Window bundles remain readable.

shortcuts.does: Picker: jump to a visible mode (iPhone is Mac only)

features.name: Auto-crop
features.says: Screen captures crop each keyframe to the window or region you worked in; uncropped frames stay in frames-full/.

config.does: Turn auto-crop off or change its settings

features.name: More than one display
features.says: The picker, overlay and capsule follow the pointer between displays; each capture belongs to one display.

features.name: Output-bound Region on Hyprland
features.says: A multi-output Hyprland capture checks that the sharing portal selected the chosen output, and a Region is cropped within its stream.
features.note: Mixed-scale Region and separate Cancel/Finish actions after output crossings were verified on an Omarchy VM and X1. A Region selected on the VM's 1.25x output also saved visible content in its movie and keyframe. The earlier X1 synthetic Cancel-to-Finish misdispatch did not recur; other Wayland portal backends and mirrored layouts are unverified.

features.name: What to record and Recent Area
features.says: A Recording setting picks what the shortcut records, including the last area drawn, reused without another drag.

config.does: What the shortcut records
The last area recorded

features.name: Screenshots
features.says: ⌥⇧4 takes a still of an area, window or screen into a one-frame bundle.

shortcuts.does: Take a screenshot (with the screenshots flag)

features.name: Draw with ⇧
features.says: Hold ⇧ and move to draw red ink over any app; it fades after release and is redrawn on the keyframes.
features.note: On Wayland the Linux preview needs the input group for ink outside its own windows.

features.name: Floating whiteboard
features.says: Open a movable, resizable paper window from the recording controls while the screen capture continues; draw, undo, clear, and close or reopen without losing strokes. The final drawing gets a dedicated contact-sheet tile and a numbered summary line.
features.note: Available from the recording controls by default on macOS and Linux. Carbon toolbar, lilac controls and mark, Host Grotesk type, and warm Paper canvas; the final drawing tile stays plain white without UI chrome. The board is captured as a window in the video, not a separate desktop-ink mark.

features.name: Microphone input equalizer
features.says: Five smooth bars respond to captured microphone samples in the Linux recording capsule; this does not assess speech or transcription quality.
features.note: On by default on Linux. The recording cue, Finish, and warning text remain separate.

features.name: Pins
features.says: ⇧-click drops a numbered pin: a brief pulse on screen, a mark on the keyframe.

features.name: Undo and cancel
features.says: Undo removes the last stroke; Esc cancels the selection or the capture.

shortcuts.does: Undo the last stroke (Ctrl+Z on Linux)

features.name: Clicks pass through
features.says: Clicks, drags and scrolls reach the app underneath and are recorded; keyframes show a ripple.
features.note: Over Wayland apps the Linux preview's click positions can be stale.

features.name: Owned GUI capture start, inspection and stop/wait
features.says: A same-user CLI atomically starts the normal interaction-aware GUI capture, waits for real frames, and stops by the request's opaque ID. Stop can wait for that capture's exact saved bundle. Retries and inspection use process-lifetime receipts, never global latest state; cancel can discard an owned pending capture. No toggle, app auto-launch or session sending.
features.note: Existing state/stop/cancel had Linux disposable-VM proof. New owned start/wait receipts have shared Rust contract tests; exact-candidate Linux GUI and Mac runtime proof are required before release. No media change or new experiment gate.

features.name: Capsule
features.says: The capsule shows the time with Finish and Cancel on the display in use; on a Mac it's a native Metal panel, black or glass.
features.note: Linux draws the GPUI capsule; glass needs macOS 26. On main, the Hyprland capsule stays pinned across workspaces without pinning other app windows.

config.does: Draw the GPUI capsule instead of the Metal one (Mac)
The Metal capsule's look

features.name: Microphone input warning
features.says: During a screen recording, the capsule says Mic unavailable, Mic stopped, or Mic very quiet when input fails, samples stop, or captured sound stays near silent. Screen recording continues; the warning does not replace recording controls.
features.note: Near-silence is not a diagnosis of microphone failure; the warning does not depend on an audio animation.

features.name: Select microphone input
features.says: Choose an input in Recording Settings or with apparent mic set; a live input meter shows its level. Keep a disconnected choice saved, explain the fallback, and use the current system default for new captures until it returns.
features.note: On PipeWire/PulseAudio Linux desktops this requires pactl and the GStreamer pulsesrc plugin. Other Linux audio servers may expose only a shared CPAL input. Windows is unsupported.

config.does: Save the chosen input; absent follows the system default

features.name: Own windows left out
features.says: The picker, ink overlay and macOS prompts stay out of Screen and Area captures. The capsule is excluded unless movableRecordingControls is on.
features.note: Prompts are a macOS case. Linux records its own windows and masks the capsule only in small keyframe-picking candidates.

features.name: Move recording controls while recording
features.says: Drag the recording capsule by its clock to expose the screen beneath it. The capsule stays visible in the captured movie and delivered full-quality keyframes.

features.name: Lower other audio (Linux experiment)
features.says: Temporarily multiplies eligible mono/stereo playback by a self-expiring gain during one capture; never snapshots or restores user volume.
features.note: Manual setup only, targeted at PipeWire 1.6.9 / WirePlumber 0.5.18. No live effectiveness indicator. Custom filter graphs, surround audio and concurrent captures are unsupported. Neutral filters remain until clients exit.

config.does: Request lowering on the next capture after manual setup and experiment opt-in
Percent of playback samples to keep; 100 skips the helper

features.name: Lower other audio
features.says: Ramps the output volume down to a set level while recording and back when it ends.
features.note: Uses CoreAudio through the helper.

config.does: Lower other audio while recording
Percent of the volume to keep

features.name: Transcribe while recording
features.says: Streams the microphone to Apple Speech during the capture, so finishing waits only for the last words.

features.name: Transcribe at pauses
features.says: On Linux, processes completed speech during recording with Parakeet and finishes the remaining audio at stop.

features.name: Keep the local recognizer warm
features.says: Lazily reuses one local Parakeet model/session across recordings, releasing it after 30 minutes idle once capture and recognition have ended.

config.does: Set false to disable cross-capture recognizer reuse at the next recording start

features.note: On by default; set warmRecognizer to false to disable at the next recording start. Linux local Parakeet pause worker only; Mac uses Apple Speech, not this engine. Retaining the recognizer costs additional idle RAM. No change to manual Paste.

features.name: Straight lines
features.says: Hold ⌥⇧ while drawing for a straight line from where the stroke began.

features.name: SwiftUI capsule
features.says: A SwiftUI capsule drawn by the helper in place of the Metal one, kept out of captures.

config.does: Which capsule to draw

features.name: Finish
features.says: Press the shortcut again or Finish; a press within 0.4 s of the start is ignored.

features.name: Local finish timing trace
features.says: Saves per-stage finish durations next to each completed bundle for debugging and performance comparisons. No transcript or screen content is added to the trace.

features.name: Copied, with a Paste chip
features.says: The summary text goes to the clipboard and the capsule shows Copied with a Paste chip; drag the chip onto a window to paste there.

features.name: Paste the latest capture
features.says: ⌥⇧V pastes the contact sheet and then the summary into the app in front.

shortcuts.does: Paste the latest capture (Alt+Shift+V on Linux)

features.name: Attach visuals after a click
features.says: The old automatic attachment rule is inactive; recorded visuals remain available through apparent zoom.

features.name: Ask the agent for an Apparent video
features.says: When enabled, a copied or pasted capture asks an agent to demonstrate complex changes in a short Apparent video if it can access the screen.

features.name: Image and text on one clipboard
features.says: Off by default: offers contact-sheet PNG and summary text together on Mac and KDE/Hyprland Wayland. Other Linux sessions copy text only. The receiver may paste only one format; inspect the unsent draft or use the explicit Paste chip and manual attachment fallback.

features.name: Guarded draft handoff
features.says: Scaffolds image-first and text-second paste with focus and attachment checks. The Linux receiver currently refuses before touching the draft because it cannot verify the editor or attachment.

features.name: Automatic original-draft handoff (blocked)
features.says: Off by default; Linux currently saves the bundle and copies summary text but refuses automatic paste because window identity cannot prove the intended draft or accepted image attachment. Attach the sheet and paste the text manually; never sends the draft.

features.name: Explain missing audio or transcription
features.says: After Stop, the completed capsule and Review distinguish missing microphone audio, saved audio with no recognized words, and a transcription failure. The handoff text reports the outcome too, without treating input level as intelligibility.

features.name: Warn when live recognition finds no words
features.says: After bounded chunks of processed audio recognize no words, warn inside the recording capsule. Check the final transcript again after Stop.

features.name: Review window
features.says: Open Latest Capture pairs the selected frame with its words and offers the full contact sheet, transcript and timeline in the same window.

features.name: Browse older captures
features.says: The review window steps through completed captures from newest to oldest without leaving the window.

features.name: Recover unbuilt captures
features.says: Saved capture assets can be recovered after the app exits unexpectedly. An interrupted recording recovers saved narration only, without reconstructing privacy-excluded screenshots.

features.name: Capture stack
features.says: The finished frame flies into a card under the capsule or at the screen edge, to drag, open or send.

features.name: Run a command per capture
features.says: Runs your own command once each bundle is written, so any agent or script can receive captures.

config.does: Command to run for each capture
Its time limit

features.name: The bundle
features.says: A .apparent folder with contact-sheet.png, frames/, summary.md, apparent.json, the recording and audio.wav.

features.name: Contact sheet and frames
features.says: Keyframes in time order, each with a number chip, the ink and click ripples drawn on, and no captions.

features.name: Keyframe selection
features.says: Keyframes are cut on marks, clicks, flags and settled screen changes, never on speech pauses: 6 up to 40 s, at most 12.

features.name: summary.md
features.says: Each keyframe line gives what was done and the words said while it was on screen, split at clause boundaries.

features.name: Spoken cues
features.says: Saying “now”, “here”, “look” or “watch” cuts a keyframe when that screen differs from the ones already chosen.
features.note: Needs measured word times, so not from a Hex transcript.

features.name: Numbered marks
features.says: Several marks on one keyframe are numbered ①② in the text, never on the image; apparent zoom --mark finds one.

features.name: Agent context
features.says: The summary names what clicks and marks land on, from Accessibility and dev-page events.

features.name: Linux element fallback
features.says: With agent context enabled, unnamed Linux clicks say element unavailable; marks keep their ink but get no OS-derived element name. Registered dev pages can supply their own context.

features.name: Text under marks
features.says: Reads the text under a mark or drag with Vision when Accessibility can't name it (with agentContext).

features.name: Apple Speech
features.says: On-device transcription with word times: SpeechAnalyzer on macOS 26, SFSpeechRecognizer on macOS 15.
features.note: Linux uses Parakeet on device.

config.does: Which engine transcribes
Apple Speech language; absent follows the Mac

features.name: Parakeet on device
features.says: Transcribes with Hex's Parakeet model, or downloads Apparent's own copy (730 MB) at first launch.

features.name: Hex
features.says: Transcribes with whichever model a running Hex has ready; falls back to Apple Speech if Hex fails.
features.note: Hex's local API is Mac only.

config.does: Hex model to use
Language sent to Hex

features.name: Your own model
features.says: Runs your own program on the audio and reads a JSON transcript from it.

config.does: Program to run
Its time limit

features.name: Legacy dev-site routing (disabled)
features.says: Old autoSend configuration is preserved, but captures now stay local and are copied; it no longer sends anything.
features.note: Retained only to document old configuration keys; no active routing.

config.does: Ignored; captures are never sent automatically

features.name: Dev-page event context (local)
features.says: The script supplies click, mark and page-error context for local captures. Its legacy session and project registration does not route captures.

features.name: Legacy smart routing (disabled)
features.says: The old routing settings remain readable; the smartRouting experiment no longer sends captures.

config.does: Ignored by capture delivery

features.name: Legacy delivery retries (disabled)
features.says: Capture processing does not queue new OpenCode deliveries. Old retry markers are not processed on startup.

features.name: Legacy agent host settings (inactive)
features.says: Older agentHost and agentOpencode settings may remain in config, but Apparent no longer copies bundles over SSH or sends captures to remote OpenCode sessions.

config.does: Legacy host value; no automatic delivery
Legacy command value; no automatic delivery

features.name: Agents on other machines
features.says: Syncs captures to remote agent hosts and pastes the remote paths.

config.does: Where captures go on the remote host

features.name: Cabled iPhone
features.says: Pick iPhone with a phone plugged in: a mirror opens, the phone's own video records with your narration, and ink works over the mirror.
features.note: Needs AVFoundation's screen capture devices.

features.name: Settings window
features.says: General, Recording, Storage, Permissions, Agents and About, from the menu's Settings….

features.name: Running build identity
features.says: Settings › About shows the package version and compiled commit, with +modified for tracked local edits and build unknown when revision metadata is unavailable.

features.name: GitHub star link
features.says: Settings › About offers a button to open Apparent's GitHub repository if you'd like to star it.

features.name: Custom shortcuts
features.says: Record new keys for Record and Paste; Apparent turns down combinations the system or another app uses, and Paste can be turned off.

config.does: Both shortcuts; paste null turns it off

features.name: Launch at login
features.says: A switch in General; the preference is stored in config.json and applied to OS login registration.

config.does: Register or unregister Apparent at login; absent leaves the OS choice alone

features.name: Microphone
features.says: Pick an input with a live level meter; a missing device falls back to the default and says so.

config.does: Chosen input; absent follows the system

features.name: Keep recordings
features.says: Video and audio go to the Trash after 7 days and whole bundles after 30; Settings › Storage picks 7, 30 days or Forever.

config.does: How long to keep media and bundles; null keeps forever

features.name: Hourly cleanup
features.says: Cleanup passes run hourly instead of daily and take zoom/ sheets with the media.

features.name: Pin a capture
features.says: apparent pin keeps a capture out of cleanup; apparent clean --dry-run shows what a pass would do.

features.name: Shrink iPhone video
features.says: A minute after a cabled capture, its video is re-encoded to HEVC at 1600 px (750 MB to 72 MB in one test).
features.note: The iPhone path is Mac only.

features.name: Choose the captures folder
features.says: Settings › Storage picks where new captures go instead of Application Support; an unusable folder falls back to the built-in one.
features.note: The Change… button is Mac only; elsewhere set capturesDir.

config.does: Where captures are written

features.name: Agent GitHub issue reporting
features.says: apparent issue previews exact text as JSON; explicit --submit publishes to tryapparent/apparent using the caller's GitHub CLI login and verifies the issue before returning its URL. No automatic capture or log attachments.
features.note: Available by default; preview stays offline unless --submit is supplied. Agents must get approval of the exact repository and text before submitting. No automatic implementation or merge.

features.name: Command-line tool
features.says: Settings › Agents installs apparent on PATH without replacing another program.
features.note: Unrelated or package-manager-owned commands are not deleted.

features.name: Timed screen recording telemetry contract
features.says: Timed CLI screen capture saves a movie and optional audio but does not collect clicks or Shift ink; new bundles mark this limitation in the manifest and summary. The app shortcut collects interactions when permission allows.

features.name: Agent skill
features.says: bunx skills add https://github.com/tryapparent/apparent/tree/main/capture/agent/skills/apparent installs the capture-reading skill; apparent skill prints it. Install the separate make-it-apparent walkthrough with its direct GitHub skill path.

features.name: apparent zoom
features.says: A dense sheet of frames around a time, a phrase that was said, or a numbered mark.

features.name: inspect and frames
features.says: Print summary.md, apparent.json or the marks; pull plain PNGs of a time range.

features.name: copy
features.says: Copy a saved capture to the clipboard without contacting an agent session. The confirmation explains that copy is text-only by default and points to the contact sheet; the user checks the unsent draft for an image.

features.name: reprocess
features.says: Rebuild a bundle with the current rules, another transcriber, or an experiment turned on.

features.name: Auto-crop playground
features.says: apparent autocrop --serve opens sliders that run the real crop on a capture and copy the settings as JSON.

features.name: apparent export
features.says: One .mp4 with ink, pins, clicks and aligned recorded audio. Missing audio requires an explicit --narration script or --no-audio choice. Opens on the whole capture for 0.5 s, then smoothly zooms toward activity; --no-zoom opts out.
features.note: Rendered with AVFoundation in the helper.

features.name: apparent export on Linux
features.says: The CLI burns ink, pins and click ripples into an MP4 with aligned WAV audio, using FFmpeg and ffprobe. Missing audio requires an explicit --narration script or --no-audio choice. Opens on the whole capture for 0.5 s before smooth activity zoom; --no-zoom opts out.
features.note: The menu export experiment remains Mac-only. Requires FFmpeg with H.264/AAC encoders; the timed CLI recorder does not collect click or ink telemetry.

features.name: Local timed export narration
features.says: Explicit --narration script generates Kokoro bm_fable speech locally for the export only; --no-audio deliberately exports silence. Sources stay unchanged.
features.note: Requires separate verified worker/model provisioning. Native platform proof remains required before release.

features.name: Export from the menu
features.says: Export Last Capture as Video… saves to ~/Movies/Apparent on Mac or a native Save dialog destination on Linux, with visible progress and failure feedback.

config.does: Show Export Last Capture as Video… (Settings › Recording › Experimental)

features.name: Copy an agent install prompt
features.says: The README offers a one-sentence prompt asking an agent to install and launch the supported desktop app from official releases.

features.name: Mac download and Homebrew
features.says: The Mac installer builds Apparent.app; a branded release has not been published yet.
features.note: No branded download or Homebrew cask has been published.

features.name: Platform-aware site download
features.says: The homepage looks up the newest published GitHub installer for the visitor's supported OS and starts its download. On lookup failure it opens the release list instead.
features.note: Mac is Apple silicon only; if the browser cannot identify the chip or Linux architecture, the button opens the release list instead. Windows has no supported installer.

features.name: Automatic updates
features.says: The Mac app updates itself with Sparkle; Check for Updates… is in the menu and Settings › About.
features.note: Mac previews use a separate Sparkle key/feed. Developer ID/notarization preparation is opt-in and awaits real-credential verification; see mac-developer-id. Linux AppImages have their own updater.

features.name: Developer ID signing and notarization setup
features.says: The Mac preview release workflow can accept a Developer ID certificate and notarization credentials without changing its update channel.
features.note: Off by default via the repository Actions variable MAC_APPLE_SIGNING_ENABLED. Preparation only: native signing, Apple acceptance and the first signed Sparkle update still require real-credential verification. This is a release switch, not an app config setting.

features.name: Linux AppImage update channels
features.says: Installed AppImages check hourly and stage a verified update for the next launch. Settings and CLI offer stable releases or nightly published main previews, a manual check with three frog result states, and live version status.

config.does: Choose the Linux release channel

config.value: { version, revision, pid, startTicks, executable, updateId, updateChannel }
config.does: Last launched process identity; verify liveness with apparent update status

features.name: Linux AppImage
features.says: AppImages for x86_64 and aarch64 (Ubuntu 24.04+), published by hand as linux-preview-N.

features.name: AUR package
features.says: yay -S apparent-linux-bin installs the AppImage with a apparent command.

features.name: Welcome tour
features.says: A welcome, an 11 s demo, one permissions checklist, an optional inline Record shortcut editor, and a first capture; it resumes where any quit left it.

config.does: Tour progress; delete it to replay the tour

features.name: Choose and try your Record shortcut
features.says: Onboarding requires an explicit shortcut choice and a successful shortcut-started recording before it can finish. Closing leaves setup unfinished for the next launch.
features.note: Default off. Desktop-owned Linux shortcuts must be explicitly accepted rather than edited. Native Mac and Linux interaction proof is required before promotion.

features.name: Drag-in permission card
features.says: For Screen Recording and Accessibility, a card flies to System Settings so you drag Apparent into the list.
features.note: Linux Wayland asks for the input group.

features.name: Reopens after a grant
features.says: If a Screen Recording grant doesn't reach the running app, Apparent reopens itself on the same screen.
features.note: Only macOS caches the grant.

features.name: macOS
features.says: Apple silicon, macOS 15 or later; live transcription and Liquid Glass need macOS 26.

features.name: Linux preview
features.says: X11, and GNOME, KDE and Hyprland on Wayland through XWayland; without the iPhone, export, OS element names, Sparkle or the tab URL. Agent context has an unnamed-click fallback.
